options.text: A change that turns a material into a brand-new substance with new properties
Something you can observe or measure without changing what the material is

items.explanation: Testing a physical property does not change a material into a different substance.

items.stem: Which property describes a material that can be flattened into a thin sheet without breaking?
items.explanation: Malleability means a material can be flattened. Ductility means it can be drawn into wire, and flexibility means it bends.

items.stem: A steel nail scratches a copper coin, but a fingernail does not. What does this show?

options.text: The fingernail is harder than the coin
The coin is harder than a fingernail but softer than steel
The coin and nail are equally hard

items.explanation: A harder material can scratch a softer material.

items.stem: A copper strip lights the bulb, but a rubber strip leaves it dark. What should cover the outside of an electrical wire?

options.text: Rubber, because it stops electric current from passing through the covering
Copper, because it carries electric current
Either material, because both are solids

items.explanation: Rubber is an electrical insulator. It helps keep current in the conducting wire and protects people from contact with the conductor.

items.stem: Why do metal pans often have wooden handles?

options.text: Wood melts at a lower temperature than metal
Wood transfers heat slowly, so the handle stays cooler

items.explanation: Wood is a poor thermal conductor compared with most metals.

items.stem: Which tool could separate iron from a mixture of iron, aluminum, and copper scraps?
items.explanation: Iron is attracted to magnets, while aluminum and copper are not attracted in this investigation.

items.stem: Three substances have different melting points: ice (0°C), wax (about 55°C), and gold (about 1,064°C). Which requires the highest temperature to begin melting?
items.explanation: Gold has the highest melting point of the three substances.

items.stem: Copper formed a wire, but glass snapped when pulled. Which property does copper demonstrate?
items.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into a wire without breaking.

items.stem: A mystery cube could be steel, glass, copper, or plastic. It is not attracted to a magnet, but it lights a bulb in a circuit. Which material is it?
items.explanation: Copper conducts electricity but is not attracted to the magnet. The other materials do not match both observations.

items.stem: A cargo ship floats while carrying 300 g of cargo. The ship and its cargo have a combined mass of 800 g. What mass of water does the floating ship displace?
items.explanation: A floating object displaces water with a weight equal to its total weight, including cargo.
